results.content:
MiniMax says its new model operates nearly 3X faster than its predecessor while reducing overall usage costs for AI agents by 70%. We’ll dig more into how teams are cutting context and token costs at VentureBeat’s Agentic Infrastructure Stack Summitin San Francisco on October 28.

But the more interesting evidence comes from independent testing: Artificial Analysis has awarded M3.1 Flash a score of 42 on its Intelligence Index, up 13 points from the previous MiniMax M3, with a per-task evaluation cost less than half that of its predecessor.

That puts M3.1 Flash on par with Z.ai's GLM-5.3 Flash, just ahead of Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash, and within striking distance ofDeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 — another new, inexpensive Chinese AI model — which scores 45. [...] MiniMax is offering M3.1 Flash through its first-party API, M Plan subscription offering and MiniMax Code desktop application.

The model costs $0.15 per million input tokens and $0.60 per million output tokens, with cached input discounted to just $0.015 per million tokens.

At those rates, a workload consuming one million uncached input tokens and producing one million output tokens would cost $0.75 in model usage charges, excluding other infrastructure or application expenses.

This makes M3.1 Flash among the cheapest frontier AI models in currently available around the world.

results.content:
## Frequently Asked Questions

What is MiniMax M3.1 Flash?  
MiniMax M3.1 Flash is an AI model released by Chinese AI company MiniMax on October 19, 2026. The company describes it as a next-generation Flash model focused on agentic tasks, coding, computer use, and cybersecurity, built to run faster and cheaper than its predecessor, MiniMax M3.

How much faster is M3.1 Flash than previous MiniMax models?  
MiniMax says online inference with M3.1 Flash is nearly three times faster than its prior generation, with reported output speeds exceeding 200 tokens per second in typical use and a median speed consistently above 170 tokens per second. [...] ## What MiniMax’s Own Announcement Says

MiniMax’s launch materials were direct about the scope of the release. In its official announcement, the company said: “Today, we officially roll out MiniMax M3.1 Flash,” framing the release as a formal production launch rather than a limited preview (MiniMax).

Describing the model’s core improvements, MiniMax said: “As a next-generation Flash model, M3.1 Flash delivers a generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, Computer Use and cybersecurity, while making online inference nearly three times faster and reducing usage costs by 70%” (MiniMax). That statement is the clearest single summary of what the company is claiming, and it is the basis for most of the launch-day coverage repeating the same speed and cost figures. [...] The headline numbers MiniMax is promoting are speed and cost, not raw intelligence scores. Online inference is said to run nearly three times faster than the prior generation, and the company says usage costs for agentic workloads fall by 70%. Those two figures matter more to enterprise buyers than any single benchmark line, because agentic workflows often require a model to make dozens or hundreds of tool calls to finish one task. When cost and latency compound across that many steps, a 70% reduction changes the economics of running an AI agent in production rather than just in a demo.

## What MiniMax M3.1 Flash Is and What Changed From M3

MiniMax pitches M3.1 Flash as a big step up for its small, fast tier. The company says an early version ran anonymously under the name "Space Bunny" and handled more than 200 trillion tokens before launch. Compared with its predecessor, MiniMax claims online inference is nearly three times faster and overall usage cost on agent tasks is about 70% lower. It also says output speed can pass 200 tokens per second, with a median above 170 (all vendor-stated, read October 20, 2026).
